paragraphs: The analytic cohort contains {cohort_sessions:,} dialysis sessions from {cohort_patients:,} patients. The recorded event prevalence is {event_prevalence_pct:.2f}%. Events are therefore less common than non-events, so accuracy alone would be an incomplete description of prediction performance.

The number of sessions is much larger than the number of patients because patients contribute repeated sessions. The project keeps each patient's sessions within one partition. The held-out test set contains {test_sessions:,} sessions from {test_patients:,} patients.

The selected {selected_model} uses {feature_count} predictors. Its test average precision is {average_precision:.3f}, ROC AUC is {roc_auc:.3f}, and Brier score is {brier_score:.3f}. At an operating threshold of {threshold:.3f}, sensitivity is {sensitivity:.1%} and precision is {precision:.1%}. Average precision and precision at the operating threshold describe different aspects of performance.

These findings describe retrospective prediction of a later low systolic blood-pressure reading. They do not establish that alerts prevent events or improve patient outcomes. External and prospective validation are still required. This academic prototype does not provide treatment recommendations.
